new_note: *And in the third week of this jubilee the unclean demons began to lead astray the children of the sons of Noah; and to make to err and destroy them.* (Jubilees 10:1). *But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?* (Matthew 3:7). The flood did not drown the spirits. Jubilees dates their return to the third week after it, leading astray the grandchildren of Noah and making them err. When John looks at the religious leaders coming down to his baptism and calls them a generation of vipers, he is naming a brood, a seed, and the same spirits that led Noah's grandchildren astray had by then made a religion out of it. The wrath to come that John warns them of is the wrath Noah's generation did not believe in either.
member_note: Jubilees 10:1 — *the unclean demons began to lead astray the children of the sons of Noah.* The leading astray that outlived the flood wears the robes John calls a generation of vipers (Matthew 3:7).

new_note: *And the days will begin to grow many and increase amongst those children of men, Till their days draw nigh to one thousand years, And to a greater number of years than (before) was the number of the days.* (Jubilees 23:27). *The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* (Matthew 11:5). Jubilees looks ahead to the days of men growing long again, back toward a thousand years, and the verses that follow fill it in: no old man, no Satan, no evil destroyer, days of blessing and healing (Jubilees 23:28–29). When John sends from prison to ask whether Yahusha (Jesus) is the one, the answer he gets is a list of bodies being mended, the blind seeing, the lame walking, the dead raised. Those are the first drops of the healing Jubilees puts at the end of the age. The King showed the signs of that restoration in his first coming and held back the rest; in Nazareth he had read Isaiah's *acceptable year of Yahuah (LORD)* and stopped before *the day of vengeance of our Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 61:2). The healing came first; the vengeance waits for his return.
member_note: Jubilees 23:27 — *Till their days draw nigh to one thousand years.* The healing of the last days, tasted first in the blind seeing and the dead raised (Matthew 11:5).

new_note: *And after this they will turn to Me in all uprightness and with all (their) heart and with all (their) soul, and I shall circumcise the foreskin of their heart and the foreskin of the heart of their seed, and I shall create in them a holy spirit, and I shall cleanse them so that they shall not turn away from Me from that day to eternity.* (Jubilees 1:23). *Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.* (Matthew 11:11). John was the greatest born of women, and yet the least in the kingdom is greater than he, not because of anything the least has done but because of what has been done in him. Jubilees names it in the Father's own words: a circumcised heart, a holy spirit created in them, a cleansing that holds from that day to eternity. Jeremiah heard the same promise as *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts* (Jeremiah 31:33), and Ezekiel as *I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes* (Ezekiel 36:27). John stood at the door of that promise and pointed at the one who brings it; the ones who walk through carry it inside them. That is the whole difference between the prophet and the least in the kingdom.
member_note: Jubilees 1:23 — *I shall circumcise the foreskin of their heart and the foreskin of the heart of their seed.* What John announced from outside, the least in the kingdom carries inside, a heart circumcised and a holy spirit created (Matthew 11:11).
flag: verdict REWORDED: the old note's Jubilees quote was a reworded form of this same verse (1:23); it describes 1:23, so the anchor holds, but the quote has been replaced with the live text.

new_note: *And their souls will cleave to Me and to all My commandments, and they will fulfil My commandments, and I shall be their Father and they will be My children.* (Jubilees 1:24). *Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.* (Matthew 11:11). Jubilees gives the order plainly. First the heart is circumcised and a holy spirit created in them (Jubilees 1:23), then their souls cleave to the commandments and fulfil them, and then He is their Father and they are His children. The keeping flows out of the new heart; it does not buy the sonship. That is what makes the least in the kingdom greater than John, not a higher rung on a ladder of works but a bond between Father and child, worked from the inside out. The commandments are not the price of the door. They are what the children of this Father do once they are in.
member_note: Jubilees 1:24 — *their souls will cleave to Me and to all My commandments, and they will fulfil My commandments.* The new heart keeps the commandments and the Father calls them children; this is what makes the least in the kingdom greater than the prophet (Matthew 11:11).

new_note: *And they will all be called children of the living Elohim (God), and every angel and every spirit will know, yea, they will know that these are My children, and that I am their Father in uprightness and righteousness, and that I love them.* (Jubilees 1:25). *Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.* (Matthew 11:11). *Children of the living Elohim (God)* is Hosea's name for the house that had been called Not My People: *in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living Elohim (God)* (Hosea 1:10), and Paul takes the same words up for the same gathering (Romans 9:26). Jubilees has the Father saying it of the ones He cleanses and circumcises in heart, and making every angel and every spirit know it. John announced that gathering; he was the voice at the edge of it. The ones inside the kingdom are the gathered themselves, known in heaven as His children, and that is why the least of them is greater than the one who pointed the way.
member_note: Jubilees 1:25 — *they will all be called children of the living Elohim (God).* Hosea's name for the house once called Not My People, known in heaven as His children; the least of them is greater than John (Matthew 11:11).

new_note: *And in this month Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day, even as lo I have declared to you all their works, that they are wicked and sinners exceedingly, and that they defile themselves and commit fornication in their flesh, and work uncleanness on the earth.* (Jubilees 16:5). *And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* (Matthew 11:23). Jubilees records what Sodom was burned for and that it stays burned until this day. Yahusha (Jesus) reaches for the same city as the measuring rod and says Capernaum will fare worse. Sodom never saw the mighty works Capernaum saw, and had it seen them it would have remained until this day; the city that watched the blind see and the dead rise and did not repent carries a heavier weight than the city whose sins were open. Sight raises the account. The judgment of Sodom is not softened here, it is the floor, and Capernaum is being told it stands below it.
member_note: Jubilees 16:5 — *He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day.* The measuring rod of judgment; Capernaum, which saw the mighty works, will fare worse than Sodom (Matthew 11:23).

new_note: *And, in like manner, Elohim (God) will execute judgment on the places where they have done according to the uncleanness of the Sodomites, like to the judgment of Sodom.* (Jubilees 16:6). *And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* (Matthew 11:23). Jubilees says the judgment of Sodom is not finished history but a pattern: Elohim (God) will execute it again wherever people do as Sodom did. Yahusha (Jesus) lays that pattern over Capernaum and then sharpens it. It will go harder with the city that saw the mighty works than with the city whose uncleanness earned the fire, because Sodom sinned without ever seeing the King, and Capernaum refused him to his face. The template Jubilees names is still in use, and the one who holds it has told us which cities fall under it.
member_note: Jubilees 16:6 — *Elohim (God) will execute judgment on the places where they have done according to the uncleanness of the Sodomites.* Sodom's judgment as a pattern still in use; Yahusha (Jesus) lays it over Capernaum (Matthew 11:23).

new_note: *And thus He created therein a sign in accordance with which they should keep Sabbath with us on the seventh day, to eat and to drink, and to bless Him who has created all things as He has blessed and sanctified to Himself a peculiar people above all peoples, and that they should keep Sabbath together with us.* (Jubilees 2:21). *For the Son of Adam is Adonai (Lord) even of the sabbath day.* (Matthew 12:8). Jubilees gives the Sabbath as a sign and says what the day is for: to eat, to drink, and to bless the One who created all things. The disciples walking through the grain, plucking ears and eating on the Sabbath, were doing exactly what the day was made for; the ones objecting had hedged the day with rules until eating became a crime. When Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam is Adonai (Lord) of the Sabbath he is not loosening the day. He is its owner telling what it is, a day for a peculiar people to eat and bless Him, not to go hungry. Jubilees was written long before those fences went up, and it already knew.
member_note: Jubilees 2:21 — *to eat and to drink, and to bless Him who has created all things.* The Sabbath as a day for eating and blessing the Creator; the Lord of the Sabbath defends his disciples' eating (Matthew 12:8).
flag: verdict REWORDED: the old note's Jubilees quote was a reworded form of this same verse (2:21); it describes 2:21, so the anchor holds, but the quote has been replaced with the live text.

new_note: *And every man who does any work thereon, or goes a journey, or tills (his) farm, whether in his house or any other place, and whoever lights a fire, or rides on any beast, or travels by ship on the sea, and whoever strikes or kills anything, or slaughters a beast or a bird, or whoever catches an animal or a bird or a fish, or whoever fasts or makes war on the Sabbaths:* (Jubilees 50:12). *How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.* (Matthew 12:12). This is the strictest Sabbath list in Jubilees, and it is worth reading what is on it: work, journeys, tilling, fire, riding, sailing, killing, hunting, fasting, war. Yahusha (Jesus) does not strike one item off the list. He points out what was never on it. Lifting a sheep out of a pit and healing a withered hand are doing well, not working, and *it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days*. The fence that had grown up around the day read *do no work* as *do no good*, and that is what he answers. Notice that Jubilees itself forbids fasting on the Sabbath; the day was for gladness and mercy from the start, and the Sabbath stands as it always has.
member_note: Jubilees 50:12 — *whoever fasts or makes war on the Sabbaths.* Jubilees' list of what the Sabbath forbids; doing well was never on it (Matthew 12:12).
flag: verdict REWORDED: the old note's Jubilees quote was a reworded form of this same verse (50:12); it describes 50:12, so the anchor holds, but the quote has been replaced with the live text. The old quote also carried the closing clause *the man who does any of these things on the Shabbat shall die*, which belongs to 50:13.

new_note: *And we did according to all His words: all the malignant evil ones we bound in the place of condemnation, and a tenth part of them we left that they might be subject before Satan on the earth.* (Jubilees 10:11). *Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.* (Matthew 12:29). At Noah's prayer the angels bound nine parts of the evil spirits in the place of condemnation and left a tenth loose on the earth under Satan. Binding is how heaven has dealt with these spirits from the beginning. When Yahusha (Jesus) says no one spoils the strong man's house without first binding the strong man, he is describing the work he was doing in front of them: the tenth that was left is being bound too, and every devil cast out is the house being spoiled. The full binding waits for the thousand years, when the angel lays hold on the dragon and binds him (Revelation 20:2), but it had already begun in Galilee.
member_note: Jubilees 10:11 — *a tenth part of them we left that they might be subject before Satan on the earth.* Nine parts bound and a tenth left loose; the strong man is bound before his house is spoiled (Matthew 12:29).
flag: verdict RE_ANCHOR_REWORDED (proposed 10:10): the old note quoted a reworded span of 10:10–11, beginning with the medicines taught to Noah (10:10). The binding and the tenth left under Satan, which is the note's real point, sit in 10:11, so the current anchor fits; the note is rebuilt on 10:11.

new_note: *And now I announce to you that the children of Yashar’el (Israel) will not keep true to this ordinance, and they will not circumcise their sons according to all this law; for in the flesh of their circumcision they will omit this circumcision of their sons, and all of them, sons of Beliar, will leave their sons uncircumcised as they were born.* (Jubilees 15:33). *Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.* (Matthew 12:31). Jubilees foresees a generation inside Yashar'el (Israel) that will not keep the sign of the covenant, and it calls them sons of Beliar, not outsiders who never heard but children of the covenant who had it in their flesh and set it aside for their sons. Of them the next verse says *there will no more be pardon or forgiveness to them* (Jubilees 15:34). That is the shape of the sin Yahusha (Jesus) says cannot be forgiven. The Pharisees had just watched the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) heal a man and called it Beelzebub; sin done in the dark is forgiven, but a covenant refused with open eyes, in front of its own evidence, is another matter.
member_note: Jubilees 15:33 — *all of them, sons of Beliar, will leave their sons uncircumcised as they were born.* The covenant refused with open eyes by its own children; the one sin Yahusha (Jesus) says is not forgiven (Matthew 12:31).
flag: verdict NOT_FOUND: the old note's quote (*great wrath from Yahuah ... because they have forsaken His covenant*) is not in the live 15:33; it describes 15:34, which carries the great wrath and the *no more pardon or forgiveness* clause the note's point rests on. The Jubilees verse may belong at 15:34; the note is rebuilt on 15:33 and quotes 15:34 inline.

new_note: *And at that time Yahuah (God) will heal His servants, And they will rise up and see great peace, And drive out their adversaries. And the righteous will see and be thankful, And rejoice with joy for ever and ever, And will see all their judgments and all their curses on their enemies.* (Jubilees 23:30). *For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.* (Matthew 12:40). Jubilees says the servants of Yahuah (God) will be healed and will rise up and see great peace. Yahusha (Jesus) gave that generation one sign: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, as Jonah was in the whale, and then up. His rising is the first of the rising Jubilees promises, the firstfruits of it, and it is the reason the rest can be counted on. The servants rise because their Master rose first, and the adversaries driven out and the peace seen afterward follow him out of the ground.
member_note: Jubilees 23:30 — *Yahuah (God) will heal His servants, And they will rise up and see great peace.* The servants rise because the Master rose first, three days and three nights in the heart of the earth (Matthew 12:40).
flag: verdict REWORDED: the old note's Jubilees quote was a reworded form of this same verse (23:30); it describes 23:30, so the anchor holds, but the quote has been replaced with the live text.

new_note: *And after this they will turn to Me in all uprightness and with all (their) heart and with all (their) soul, and I shall circumcise the foreskin of their heart and the foreskin of the heart of their seed, and I shall create in them a holy spirit, and I shall cleanse them so that they shall not turn away from Me from that day to eternity.* (Jubilees 1:23). *Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.* (Matthew 12:45). A house swept and empty is the picture of a man delivered with nothing put inside him. Jubilees names what must go in: a heart circumcised, a holy spirit created in them, a cleansing that keeps them from turning away. Casting out is half the work; the other half is the Father making the house His own so there is no room when the seven come back. That generation had the devils cast out in front of them and would not take the new heart, and Yahusha (Jesus) says its last state will be worse than the first. Deliverance without the Father moving in is only a vacancy.
member_note: Jubilees 1:23 — *I shall create in them a holy spirit, and I shall cleanse them.* What must fill the swept house, or the seven return (Matthew 12:45).
flag: verdict REWORDED: the old note's Jubilees quote was a reworded form of this same verse (1:23); it describes 1:23, so the anchor holds, but the quote has been replaced with the live text.

new_note: *And their souls will cleave to Me and to all My commandments, and they will fulfil My commandments, and I shall be their Father and they will be My children.* (Jubilees 1:24). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). Yahusha (Jesus) names his family by one mark: whoever does the will of my Father. Jubilees had already given the Father's own words for the same bond: their souls cleave to Me and to all My commandments, they fulfil My commandments, I am their Father and they are My children. The will of the Father is not a mystery hovering somewhere above the commandments; it is the commandments. John says it the same way later, *hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments* (1 John 2:3). The kingdom family is known by what it does, and what it does is keep the Father's Torah from a cleaving heart.
member_note: Jubilees 1:24 — *I shall be their Father and they will be My children.* The Father's children are the ones who cleave to His commandments; the same mark names the King's family (Matthew 12:50).

new_note: *And the prince Mastêmâ sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land, in order to destroy the land, and rob the children of men of their labours. Before they could plough in the seed, the ravens picked (it) from the surface of the ground.* (Jubilees 11:11). *And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up:* (Matthew 13:4). Jubilees shows the ravens as no accident of nature: the prince Mastema sent them to eat the seed before it could be ploughed in, to rob men of their labour, and the boy Abram drove them off seventy times in a day (Jubilees 11:19–20). When Yahusha (Jesus) explains his own parable he says the fowls are no accident either: *then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart* (Matthew 13:19). The birds on the way side are the same birds, sent by the same prince, after the same seed. The parable is not borrowing a farming picture; it is describing a war Jubilees had already named.
member_note: Jubilees 11:11 — *the prince Mastêmâ sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land.* The birds that devour the seed were sent; the fowls by the way side are the wicked one (Matthew 13:4, 19).
flag: verdict REWORDED: the old note's Jubilees quote was a reworded form of this same verse (11:11); it describes 11:11, so the anchor holds, but the quote has been replaced with the live text.

new_note: *And it came to pass when the children of men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them, that the angels of Elohim (God) saw them on a certain year of this jubilee, that they were beautiful to look upon; and they took themselves wives of all whom they chose, and they bare to them sons and they were giants.* (Jubilees 5:1). *But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.* (Matthew 13:25). The enemy sowed while men slept, and the first sowing was in the days when the angels of Elohim (God) took wives of the daughters of men and bred giants. Jubilees names it here, 1 Enoch tells it at length (1 Enoch 6), and Genesis 6 keeps it. The tares are not a figure for bad ideas; the parable says they are the children of the wicked one (Matthew 13:38), and this is where that seed first entered the field. No one saw it coming. Men slept, and woke to giants.
member_note: Jubilees 5:1 — *they took themselves wives of all whom they chose, and they bare to them sons and they were giants.* The first tares sown in the field while men slept (Matthew 13:25).
flag: verdict REWORDED: the old note's Jubilees quote was a reworded form of this same verse (5:1); it describes 5:1, so the anchor holds, but the quote has been replaced with the live text.

new_note: *For owing to these three things came the flood upon the earth, namely, owing to the fornication wherein the Watchers against the law of their ordinances went a whoring after the daughters of men, and took themselves wives of all which they chose: and they made the beginning of uncleanness.* (Jubilees 7:21). *The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one;* (Matthew 13:38). Noah tells his sons why the flood came: the Watchers went whoring after the daughters of men against the law of their ordinances, and from that uncleanness came the giants who devoured one another (Jubilees 7:22). Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples what the tares are: the children of the wicked one, planted in the same field as the children of the kingdom. Noah's account shows a seed that was never the Father's, growing beside the sons of Adam and devouring them. The flood cut it down once; the parable says it grows again in the field of the world, and the reapers wait for the harvest.
member_note: Jubilees 7:21 — *the Watchers against the law of their ordinances went a whoring after the daughters of men.* The seed that was never the Father's; the tares are the children of the wicked one (Matthew 13:38).

new_note: *And in the first (year) of the third jubilee, Cain slew Abel because Elohim (God) accepted the sacrifice of Abel, and did not accept the offering of Cain.* (Jubilees 4:2). *The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one;* (Matthew 13:38). The first tare in the field was Cain. Jubilees says plainly why he killed: Elohim (God) accepted Abel's sacrifice and not his offering. John writes the same thing in the parable's own words, *not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother* (1 John 3:12). When Yahusha (Jesus) says the tares are the children of the wicked one, he is not inventing a category; he is naming a line that begins in the first family and runs through the field of the world to the harvest. The two seeds were there from the beginning, and the first field they shared was a literal one.
member_note: Jubilees 4:2 — *Cain slew Abel because Elohim (God) accepted the sacrifice of Abel.* The first of the children of the wicked one, *who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother* (1 John 3:12; Matthew 13:38).
flag: verdict REWORDED: the old note's Jubilees quote was a reworded form of this same verse (4:2); it describes 4:2, so the anchor holds, but the quote has been replaced with the live text.

new_note: *For Ishmael and his sons and his brothers and Esau, Yahuah (God) did not cause to approach Him, and he chose them not because they are the children of Abraham, because He knew them, but He chose Yashar’el (Israel) to be His people.* (Jubilees 15:30). *And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil.* (Matthew 15:22). Not every child of Abraham is the chosen seed. Jubilees says it flat: Ishmael, his sons, his brothers, Esau, Yahuah (God) did not bring them near, though they were Abraham's children; He chose Yashar'el (Israel) to be His people. The woman of Canaan crying *Son of David* is standing outside that choice, and Yahusha (Jesus) does not pretend otherwise: *I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 15:24). Her story matters because he does not erase the line. He keeps it, and still has mercy at the edge of it, where the crumbs fall.
member_note: Jubilees 15:30 — *he chose them not because they are the children of Abraham, because He knew them, but He chose Yashar’el (Israel).* Not every child of Abraham is the chosen seed; the woman of Canaan stands outside the line the King keeps (Matthew 15:22).

new_note: *And He sanctified it, and gathered it from amongst all the children of men ; for there are many nations and many peoples, and all are His, and over all has He placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from Him.* (Jubilees 15:31). *But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.* (Matthew 15:26). Jubilees explains the difference between the children and the dogs. Many nations and many peoples are all His, but over them He set spirits in authority, and those spirits lead them astray; Yashar'el (Israel) He sanctified and gathered out from among all the children of men to rule Himself. Moses sang the same thing: *when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel). For the LORD’S portion is his people* (Deuteronomy 32:8–9). The woman of Canaan comes from under one of those spirits, and her daughter is vexed with a devil to prove it. Yahusha (Jesus) names the line before he crosses it with mercy; the bread belongs to the household the Father rules directly.
member_note: Jubilees 15:31 — *over all has He placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from Him.* The nations under spirits, Yashar'el (Israel) gathered out to be ruled directly; the children's bread (Matthew 15:26).

new_note: *But over Yashar’el (Israel) He did not appoint any angel or spirit, for He alone is their ruler, and He will preserve them and require them at the hand of His angels and His spirits, and at the hand of all His powers in order that He may preserve them and bless them, and that they may be His and He may be theirs from henceforth for ever.* (Jubilees 15:32). *But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.* (Matthew 15:26). Over Yashar'el (Israel) no angel and no spirit: He alone is their ruler, and He keeps them Himself and requires them at the hand of every power. That is why Yahusha (Jesus) says he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) (Matthew 15:24). The Shepherd who said through Ezekiel *I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out* (Ezekiel 34:11) had come to do it in person. The woman of Canaan is not of that flock, and he tells her so. Then he feeds her anyway, at the crumbs, because the Father who rules Yashar'el (Israel) directly is also the one to whom all the nations belong. The line is kept, and mercy crosses it without erasing it.
member_note: Jubilees 15:32 — *over Yashar’el (Israel) He did not appoint any angel or spirit, for He alone is their ruler.* The flock the Father shepherds Himself; the children's bread is theirs, and mercy still reaches the crumbs (Matthew 15:26).

new_note: *And (that) all the seed of his sons should be nations, and be reckoned with the nations; but from the sons of Isaac one should become a holy seed, and should not be reckoned among the nations.* (Jubilees 16:17). *But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.* (Matthew 15:26). Abraham's other sons became nations and are reckoned with the nations; from Isaac comes one holy seed that is not reckoned among them. Paul says it the same way: *they are not all Yashar'el (Israel), which are of Yashar'el (Israel) ... In Isaac shall thy seed be called* (Romans 9:6–7). Children and dogs at the table is the same distinction. The seed of promise has a name and a line, and the woman of Canaan is not in it, and Yahusha (Jesus) says so to her face. He does not lie to her to be kind; he keeps the line and then feeds her at it.
member_note: Jubilees 16:17 — *from the sons of Isaac one should become a holy seed, and should not be reckoned among the nations.* The holy seed not reckoned among the nations; the children's bread (Matthew 15:26).

The old quote also carried *For he should become the portion of Yahuah (God) most High*, which belongs to 16:18.

new_note: *And after this law I made known to you the days of the Sabbaths in the desert of Sinai, which is between Elim and Sinai.* (Jubilees 50:1). *And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full.* (Matthew 15:37). The seven baskets are not a random count. Jubilees closes with the Sabbaths made known in the desert of Sinai, days and years and jubilees all built on seven. The first feeding left twelve baskets, a basket for every tribe (Matthew 14:20); the second leaves seven, the number of the Sabbath and the finished week. The King who fed the crowds counts the way Sinai counts, in twelves for the tribes and in sevens for rest. A people raised on that count would have noticed what was left over.
member_note: Jubilees 50:1 — *I made known to you the days of the Sabbaths in the desert of Sinai.* The Sabbaths built on seven; the second feeding leaves seven baskets (Matthew 15:37).

new_note: *And I told you of the Sabbaths of the land on Mount Sinai, and I told you of the jubilee years in the sabbaths of years: but the year thereof have I not told you till you enter the land which you are to possess.* (Jubilees 50:2). *And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full.* (Matthew 15:37). Jubilees counts the land's rest in sevens: Sabbaths of years, and the jubilee at the end of seven sevens, as Moses laid it out, *seven sabbaths of years unto thee, seven times seven years* (Leviticus 25:8). The two feedings count in the two numbers of Yashar'el (Israel): twelve baskets for the twelve tribes (Matthew 14:20), seven baskets for the Sabbath and the jubilee. A crowd fed and filled with seven baskets over is a picture of the rest the land was promised: enough, more than enough, and the count of the week on top. The bread was real, and so was the number.
member_note: Jubilees 50:2 — *I told you of the jubilee years in the sabbaths of years.* The jubilee counted in sevens; seven baskets left over at the second feeding (Matthew 15:37).

new_note: *Wherefore I have ordained for you the year-weeks and the years and the jubilees: there are forty-nine jubilees from the days of Adam until this day, and one week and two years and there are yet forty years to come (lit. "distant for learning the commandments of Yahuah (God), until they pass over into the land of Canaan, crossing the Jordan to the west.* (Jubilees 50:4). *And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full.* (Matthew 15:37). Jubilees counts forty-nine jubilees from Adam to the border of the land, seven sevens of jubilees, with the fiftieth opening as Yashar'el (Israel) crosses Jordan. Seven is the number this book counts the world's history in. When Yahusha (Jesus) feeds the crowd and seven baskets remain, the number lands on ears trained by that count. He had already stood in Nazareth and read *the acceptable year of Yahuah (Lord)* and told them *this day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears* (Luke 4:19, 21); the jubilee had a face. The seven baskets are the full measure left over when the jubilee is proclaimed.
member_note: Jubilees 50:4 — *there are forty-nine jubilees from the days of Adam until this day.* The world counted in sevens from Adam; seven baskets over when the jubilee has a face (Matthew 15:37).

new_note: *And Yahuah (God) said to us: “It is not good that the man should be alone: let us make a helpmeet for him.”* (Jubilees 3:4). *And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female,* (Matthew 19:4). When the Pharisees ask about divorce, Yahusha (Jesus) does not go to Moses first. He goes behind Moses to the beginning, and Jubilees tells that beginning in the Father's own words to the angels: it is not good that the man should be alone, let us make a helpmeet for him. The one who made them male and female made them for each other, and that is the standard; what Moses allowed *because of the hardness of your hearts* (Matthew 19:8) sat under it, not over it. Both are Torah, and neither cancels the other. The King reads Torah from its first page and the hard hearts from the page where Moses met them.
member_note: Jubilees 3:4 — *It is not good that the man should be alone: let us make a helpmeet for him.* The beginning the King reads from before he reads Moses (Matthew 19:4).

new_note: *And He awaked Adam out of his sleep and on awaking he rose on the sixth day, and He brought her to him, and he knew her, and said to her: “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she will be called my wife; because she was taken from her husband.”* (Jubilees 3:6). *And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?* (Matthew 19:5). Adam wakes, she is brought to him, and he says it: bone of my bones, flesh of my flesh, taken from her husband. That is why there is a *for this cause*. A man cleaves to his wife and the two are one flesh because she was one flesh with him before she was ever separate from him. Yahusha (Jesus) quotes Genesis to the Pharisees, and Jubilees carries the same scene in the same words. Marriage is a return to one body that was divided; what Elohim (God) joined on the sixth day no court was made to split.
member_note: Jubilees 3:6 — *This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she will be called my wife.* One flesh because she was taken from him; the *for this cause* of Matthew 19:5.

new_note: *And after this they will turn to Me from amongst the nations with all their heart and with all their soul and with all their strength, and I shall gather them from amongst all the nations, and they will seek Me, so that I shall be found of them, when they seek Me with all their heart and with all their soul.* (Jubilees 1:15). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). Twelve thrones judging twelve tribes means twelve tribes will be there to be judged. Jubilees says how they get there: they turn to Him from among the nations with all their heart, and He gathers them from among all the nations. That is Ezekiel's two sticks made one, and Isaiah's *outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel)* and *dispersed of Yahudah (Judah)* gathered *from the four corners of the earth* (Isaiah 11:12). The regeneration Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of is a gathered people of Jacob's blood seated under Jacob's sons' names, not a church that has renamed itself Yashar'el (Israel). The scattering was real, the gathering is real, and the thrones are for real tribes.
member_note: Jubilees 1:15 — *I shall gather them from amongst all the nations.* The gathering that puts twelve tribes under twelve thrones (Matthew 19:28).

new_note: *And they will be princes and judges, and chiefs of all the seed of the sons of Jacob; They will speak the word of Yahuah (God) in righteousness, And they will judge all His judgments in righteousness. And they will declare My ways to Jacob And My paths to Yashar’el (Israel). The blessing of Yahuah (God) will be given in their mouths To bless all the seed of the beloved.* (Jubilees 31:15). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). Isaac's blessing on Levi at Bethel is a blessing of judgeship: princes and judges and chiefs over all the seed of Jacob's sons, speaking the word of Yahuah (God) and declaring His ways to Jacob. Yahusha (Jesus) seats twelve men on twelve thrones over the same seed. Judging in Yashar'el (Israel) was never only a courtroom; *Yahuah (LORD) raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them* (Judges 2:16). What Levi was blessed to carry at the altar, the twelve are given to carry at the throne, and the people under them are still the seed of the sons of Jacob.
member_note: Jubilees 31:15 — *they will be princes and judges, and chiefs of all the seed of the sons of Jacob.* Levi's blessing of judgeship over Jacob's seed; twelve thrones over the twelve tribes (Matthew 19:28).

new_note: *And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way, alike men and cattle and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth-all of them corrupted their ways and their orders, and they began to devour each other, and lawlessness increased on the earth and every imagination of the thoughts of all men (was) thus evil continually.* (Jubilees 5:2). *But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:37). Yahusha (Jesus) says his coming will look like Noah's days, and Jubilees says what Noah's days looked like: lawlessness increased on the earth, and all flesh corrupted its way, down to the cattle and the birds, every order out of its order. The word is lawlessness, Torah thrown off, and it is the same word the King uses for the end, *because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold* (Matthew 24:12). The sign of the end is not a world that never heard the law. It is a world that had it and corrupted its way, and a religion that teaches its people the law is done away with is not a bystander to that sign.
member_note: Jubilees 5:2 — *lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way.* The days of Noah were days of lawlessness; so will the coming of the Son of Adam be (Matthew 24:37).

new_note: *And as for all those who corrupted their ways and their thoughts before the flood, no man’s person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted in behalf of his sons, whom Elohim (God) saved from the waters of the flood on his account; for his heart was righteous in all his ways, according as it was commanded regarding him, and he had not departed from aught that was ordained for him.* (Jubilees 5:19). *For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark,* (Matthew 24:38). Before the flood no one's person was accepted but Noah's, and his sons were saved on his account. Everyone else was eating, drinking, marrying, ordinary life, *and knew not until the flood came, and took them all away* (Matthew 24:39). The ones the flood took are the ones taken; Noah was the one left. So when Yahusha (Jesus) goes on to say one shall be taken and the other left, the pattern he has just set up is the flood, and when the disciples ask where the taken go, the answer is *wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together* (Luke 17:37). Being taken is not the rescue. The accepted one is the one still standing when the water goes down.
member_note: Jubilees 5:19 — *no man’s person was accepted save that of Noah alone.* The one accepted was the one left; the flood took the rest (Matthew 24:38).

new_note: *And after this they will turn to Me from amongst the nations with all their heart and with all their soul and with all their strength, and I shall gather them from amongst all the nations, and they will seek Me, so that I shall be found of them, when they seek Me with all their heart and with all their soul.* (Jubilees 1:15). *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). The Father says He will gather them from among all the nations when they turn with all their heart and all their soul and all their strength, the words of the Shema (Deuteronomy 6:5) and of Jeremiah's promise, *ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart* (Jeremiah 29:13). Then the Son sends his disciples to all nations. The two fit together. The sheep are scattered through every nation, so the shepherds are sent through every nation; *teach all nations* is not a change of subject from the gathering of Yashar'el (Israel), it is how the gathering is carried out, because that is where the lost sheep are. The door is wide because the scattering was wide.
member_note: Jubilees 1:15 — *they will turn to Me from amongst the nations with all their heart and with all their soul.* The gathering from among all nations, carried out by sending to all nations (Matthew 28:19).

new_note: *And after this they will turn to Me in all uprightness and with all (their) heart and with all (their) soul, and I shall circumcise the foreskin of their heart and the foreskin of the heart of their seed, and I shall create in them a holy spirit, and I shall cleanse them so that they shall not turn away from Me from that day to eternity.* (Jubilees 1:23). *Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.* (Matthew 28:20). The last words of Matthew are a command to teach commandments. Jubilees tells how a gathered people will be able to keep them: a circumcised heart, a holy spirit created in them, a cleansing that holds. Jeremiah calls it *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts* (Jeremiah 31:33); Ezekiel calls it *I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes* (Ezekiel 36:27). The commission is that same work of the heart going out: baptize them, then teach them to observe everything he commanded. He opened his teaching by saying *one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law* (Matthew 5:18) and closed it by sending men to teach the keeping of it. Grace is not the end of the commandments; it is the heart that can finally keep them.
member_note: Jubilees 1:23 — *I shall cleanse them so that they shall not turn away from Me from that day to eternity.* The new heart that keeps what the disciples are sent to teach (Matthew 28:20).

new_note: *And they will all be called children of the living Elohim (God), and every angel and every spirit will know, yea, they will know that these are My children, and that I am their Father in uprightness and righteousness, and that I love them.* (Jubilees 1:25). *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). *Children of the living Elohim (God)* is the name Hosea gave to the house that had been called Not My People: *in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living Elohim (God)* (Hosea 1:10), and Paul quotes it for the same gathering (Romans 9:26). Jubilees has the Father using the name for the ones He gathers and cleanses, and making every angel and spirit know it. The commission goes to all nations because that is the place where it was said to them *not my people*; that is where they were sown. The disciples are sent to find the Father's children where they were scattered, so that what heaven already knows about them becomes their own.
member_note: Jubilees 1:25 — *they will know that these are My children, and that I am their Father.* Hosea's sons of the living Elohim (God), sought where they were scattered (Matthew 28:19).

new_note: *And we did according to all His words: all the malignant evil ones we bound in the place of condemnation, and a tenth part of them we left that they might be subject before Satan on the earth.* (Jubilees 10:11). *But when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him all his armour wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils.* (Luke 11:22). Nine parts were bound at Noah's prayer and a tenth left loose on the earth under Satan. Satan is the strong man armed, keeping his palace with that tenth. Yahusha (Jesus) had just cast a devil out of a dumb man (Luke 11:14), and he tells them what it means: a stronger one has come upon him, overcome him, taken the armour he trusted in, and is dividing the spoils. The binding that began in Noah's day is being finished by the one stronger than Satan; every devil cast out is spoil carried from a house whose master is already beaten. The last of the binding waits for the thousand years (Revelation 20:2).
member_note: Jubilees 10:11 — *all the malignant evil ones we bound in the place of condemnation.* The binding begun at Noah's prayer, finished by the stronger one who divides the spoils (Luke 11:22).

new_note: *And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way, alike men and cattle and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth-all of them corrupted their ways and their orders, and they began to devour each other, and lawlessness increased on the earth and every imagination of the thoughts of all men (was) thus evil continually.* (Jubilees 5:2). *They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.* (Luke 17:27). Luke gives the surface of Noah's days: eating, drinking, marrying, until the ark door closed. Jubilees gives what was under the surface: lawlessness increasing, all flesh corrupting its way, every imagination of the thoughts of all men evil continually. The ordinary life Yahusha (Jesus) describes was not innocent. It was carrying on as usual on top of that corruption, deaf to the hammer on the ark. That is the warning for the day of the Son of Adam: not that people will be eating and marrying, but that they will be doing it with the law thrown off and the judgment already appointed, and never look up.
member_note: Jubilees 5:2 — *every imagination of the thoughts of all men (was) thus evil continually.* What lay under the eating and drinking of Noah's days (Luke 17:27).
